steps.message:
Route the overhead MEP of the hardest hall in the corpus, clash-free (dc_model hall_seed005_d100)

Situation

You are the MEP coordinator for a data hall — and this one is deliberately difficult. The room is ~27 × 24 m with 94 cabinets, and its 7200 mm structural grid is offset 150 mm from the floor-tile grid, so a cabinet cannot be both on-tile and clear of the columns — you must resolve that conflict the way a coordinator would. A circulation cross-aisle re-registers every cabinet row, and 104 sprinkler heads crowd the ceiling your routes must thread through. The architect has issued a seven-sheet drawing set and you must produce the coordinated 3D model: rebuild the room and its fit-out exactly as drawn, then route the three overhead services through the plenum so that nothing collides, every row is served, and the routes are as short as practical — the job a BIM coordinator does before construction, delivered as an IFC4 model built by a script.

Inputs (under input/ — seven PNG drawing sheets, nothing else)

A-101 equipment plan · A-301 building section · A-601 cabinet schedule · A-602 containment/pathway/construction data · M-101 chilled water · E-101 busway & PDU · F-101 sprinkler grid.

They behave like a real drawing set: positions on the plan, sizes in the schedule, elevations only in the section callout. No JSON side-channel, no coordinate dump. Reconcile them yourself (read them as images).

Goal

Rebuild the hall as the coordination background: racks on their floor tiles with correct facings, structural columns, CRAHs, PDUs, access floor, containment, and every sprinkler head — your routes are clash-checked against all of it.

Route three overhead services from the entries marked on M-101/E-101 — telecom cable tray, power busway, chilled-water pipe — as straight axis-aligned segments (every direction or tier change is a new segment). Tray and busway must serve every rack row; chilled water must serve every row and reach every CRAH, including the perimeter units no row header passes.

Constraints (all checked mechanically)

Zero hard clashes — one solid overlapping another by > 2 mm anywhere (a tray through a column, a pipe through a rack) fails the task. Columns run full clear height.

Connectivity — each service must form ONE connected network reaching its service entry; every row served along ≥ 80 % of its length by all three services (within 2500 mm across the row); chilled water within 2500 mm of every CRAH.

Code compliance — 2600 mm min headroom; 460 mm kept clear below every sprinkler deflector (plus the NFPA 13 obstruction rule within 450 mm below a deflector); heads required beneath runs wider than 1200 mm and beneath containment roofs; 300 mm separation between tray and busway on at least one axis; no chilled water in the 1800 mm dedicated space above a PDU; 25.4 mm pipe insulation counts in clashes. The under-floor plenum is usable for routing.

Modelling contract — IFC4 via ifcopenshell==0.8.4 (+ numpy only), millimetre project units (but placement-matrix translations in metres!), 2D profile points only, the prescribed spatial structure, exact element classes (e.g. racks = IfcFurniture/USERDEFINED/"Rack") and the required Pset_DCM_* property sets, correct facing rotations about the footprint centre. Validate with express_rules=True before submitting. The script must run headless in 300 s, deterministically, with no network and no reading the PNGs back — bake everything you read off the drawings into the script as literals.

Expected output

One self-contained Python script at output/solution.py that builds the model with ifcopenshell and writes one IFC4 file to sys.argv[1] (default output/model.ifc).

Scoring: schema gate → clash gate → connectivity gate (each 0 if failed), then score = compliance × min(1, L_opt / L_yours) — material efficiency against the reference route, discounted by code violations.

Additional requirements

In addition to the original modelling, routing, clash, connectivity and code-compliance obligations, the solver shall also produce the following design-quality data.  These items do not change the primary score; they are reported as diagnostics.

1. Achieved clearances
For every sprinkler head, compute and make available the vertical clearance from the top of each service (tray, busway, CHW) that passes under it.  For every PDU, compute the vertical clearance from the top of the PDU to the nearest CHW pipe.  For every tray-busway pair, compute the minimum separation on any axis.  The values may be stored as Pset properties on the relevant elements or simply realised by the geometry so the host grader can measure them.

2. Under-floor versus overhead length split
For each of the three services report (or make measurable from geometry) the centreline length that runs entirely below finished floor and the centreline length that runs in the overhead plenum.  The under-floor plenum remains usable; this requirement only asks that the split be visible.

3. Service elevation / tier assignment
Place every route segment so that its elevation relative to finished floor is unambiguous.  Prefer the clear-height band defined on the drawings (finished floor to the 2600 mm minimum clear height).  The grader will measure how much of each service lies inside that band, above it, or below finished floor.

4. Support / hanger elements (optional; reported when present)
If the drawings call out a maximum support spacing (for example the 1500 mm busway support limit on E-101), place support or hanger elements at intervals that respect that limit, or report the maximum unsupported span that remains.  Supports may be modelled as IfcElementAssembly or IfcBuildingElementProxy with ObjectType containing "Support" or "Hanger".

5. Service drops / terminations (optional)
In addition to the existing row-coverage obligation, provide explicit drop or termination points that bring each service to the cabinets or CRAHs it serves.  Model drops as short vertical or short horizontal segments (or as distinct elements whose ObjectType contains "Drop", "Tap" or "Termination").  The grader counts them and records their locations.

6. Drawing-note reconciliation log (optional side file)
Write a small JSON file next to the IFC (output/reconciliation.json) that lists every numeric clearance, size or spacing note extracted from the seven drawing sheets and states how it was applied (or why it could not be applied).  Example entries: "A-301 clear height 2600 mm -> enforced as headroom rule", "E-101 busway support 1500 mm max -> supports placed at 1400 mm centres".  Absence of the file is not a gate failure; its presence is reported.

All gates, the modelling contract, the runtime limit and the primary score formula remain exactly as stated above.  The additional data above are diagnostics only.

steps.message:
Implemented and verified the deliverables:

- [solution.py](/app/files/dc_model__hall_seed005_d100__mep_routing/output/solution.py)  
  Self-contained IFC4 generator. It creates the hall background, 94 racks, 104 sprinklers, structural columns, CRAHs, PDUs, access floor, three service networks, drops, supports, clearance properties, and routing diagnostics.

- [model.ifc](/app/files/dc_model__hall_seed005_d100__mep_routing/output/model.ifc)  
  Generated IFC4 model with 15,436 entities. Counts include 94 `IfcFurniture` racks, 104 sprinkler terminals, 52 pipe segments, 20 cable carrier segments, 16 CRAHs, 16 columns, 4 PDUs, and 302 proxy drop/support elements.

- [reconciliation.json](/app/files/dc_model__hall_seed005_d100__mep_routing/output/reconciliation.json)  
  Records the extracted clear-height, tile-grid, sprinkler, support-spacing, insulation, and service-separation notes and their application.

Verification completed with `py_compile`, IFC reopening, and `ifcopenshell.validate(..., express_rules=True)`, which returned zero validation errors.
